messages:
maria: Heads up — Sec is planning an egress + IAM conditional change for the keystore/privatelink next Tue morning (eu-west-1). This will add stricter aws:SourceIp and require VPC endpoint authentication. Could affect GPU warm-pool joins and decrypt calls.

aj: Do we have a concrete policy snippet? what's the rollback window?

leigh: The plan: 1) tighten SGs on privatelink endpoints, 2) add IAM Condition: aws:SourceIp + aws:ViaAWSService for internal bootstrap, 3) increase keystore audit retention to 365d. Rollout will be staged by region, canary in staging then eu-west-1 prod. Rollback window 30m after canary.

sre_jun: Noted. We saw a 503 decrypt timeout pattern last week during NATGW flaps that caused node eviction and warm pool depletion. If keystore denies or times out, GPU nodes fail init and sit in 'joining' for ~2m then get ejected.

maria: Example log we saw (from last week):
```
2026-02-07T09:18:12Z kubelet[info] keystore: decrypt request failed: context deadline exceeded (attempt 1/3)
2026-02-07T09:20:34Z node-manager[warn] node join failed: keystore decrypt timeout -> cordon + drain triggered
```

aj: That matches. If we add aws:SourceIp and tighten privatelink SGs, some ephemeral ENIs and node bootstrap traffic might be blocked if routes/NATs are mis-specified. Need a test matrix.

leigh: Agreed. Proposed mitigations: - pre-authorize staging and prod warm-pool subnets' CIDR on the keystore policy, - enable a short-lived fallback cache that serves bootstrap keys for 5m, - run a targeted canary with 3 nodes in a dedicated subnet.

sre_jun: +1 for fallback cache. How do we revoke that later safely?

maria: Fallback cache would be a temporary signed-token store using short TTLs (120s default, bumped to 300s for rollout). Revoke by removing token issuer role from keystore. We'll document the exact revoke steps in runbook.

aj: Cost question: keeping the fallback cache in front of keystore adds an extra Redis instance and some egress. Rough estimate: ~120USD/day while active in eu-west-1. Can we avoid cost by using an in-node ephemeral cache?

leigh: In-node ephemeral cache is riskier for audits. Security wants audit lines for every decrypt attempt — cache hits must still log identity and token id. So central short-lived cache is preferred.

ops-bot: Scheduling note: infra-deploy bot will attempt privileged IAM policy change on 2026-02-12T03:00 UTC to eu-west-1 after successful canary. Manual approval required at canary+15m.

maria: Action items I propose: 1) Infra: create canary subnets + pre-authorize CIDRs in keystore policy (aj), 2) SRE: add fallback cache + runbook with revoke steps (sre_jun), 3) Sec: prepare new IAM Condition policy + audit retention change (leigh), 4) Product Ops: communicate possible 1% risk of short warm-pool join failures during rollout (maria).

aj: I'll open infra ticket and attach terraform snippet for the CIDR pre-auth: 
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_policy" "keystore_conditional" {
  name = "keystore-conditional-eu"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow",
      Action = ["kms:Decrypt"],
      Resource = "*",
      Condition = { "IpAddress": { "aws:SourceIp": ["10.40.16.0/22","10.40.20.0/24"] }}
    }]
  })
}
```

sre_jun: I'll prototype fallback cache using Redis with a very narrow IAM principal and emit audit events to the central collector. Will also add metric: keystore.decrypt.latency and warmpool.join.failures.

leigh: For audit retention change, we need compliance signoff. I submitted PR to the compliance tracker: https://redwood.internal/compliance/PR-8481 — please review.

maria: Can we schedule a 30m playbook dry-run Friday prior to Tue rollout? We run the canary and then do a simulated revoke to validate the rollback steps.

aj: Friday dry-run scheduled 2026-02-09 10:00 UTC. I'll invite subsystems: infra, sre, sec, deploy.

ops-bot: @channel Reminder: create an on-call rotation for the rollout window and add deploy-bot to approvals.

deploy-bot: Manual approval required for prod changes. Approvers: @leigh, @maria.

maria: TL;DR: Tighten IAM/egress on keystore next Tue. Risk: short GPU warm-pool join failures -> plan: canary + fallback cache + dry-run + revoke playbook. Owners assigned above. :thumbsup:

leigh: A few follow-ups: 1) add explicit NAT egress rules for canary subnet, 2) verify KMS key grants across accounts, 3) ensure CloudTrail logs include keystore:Decrypt events with requesterIdentity.

aj: I'll attach the NAT egress rule diff to the infra ticket. Will also add a check in the preflight CI to ensure keystore endpoints resolve from canary subnets.

sre_jun: Will create alert: if warmpool.join.failures > 2 within 10m during rollout, abort and rollback IAM policy.

maria: Thanks team. I'll update the rollout doc after dry-run and ping here when we flip the canary.

leigh: Acknowledged.
